separates: throwaway, first-retained, later-retained, missing-key, retry, and retained-q50 disagreements
does_not_separate: runtime, CPU, or source mechanism names
acceptance_rule: every generated key has a stable row id, generated/retained flag, key index, failure/retry/missing status, and aggregate membership
if_missing: aggregate q50 can hide first-key or missing-key effects
collector: benchmark JSON plus reporter raw rows

acceptance_rule: each row records helper API, requested delay, observed keydown-to-keyup duration, keyup-to-next-keydown gap, event counts, and browser revision
if_missing: held-key, tap, and complete-keypress rows can be accidentally pooled
collector: Playwright wrapper plus browser event trace

separates: ordering-marker claims around rich-text persistence and timer rewrites
does_not_separate: whether callback work moved between measurement slices
acceptance_rule: timer callback, persistence marker, keydown, input, keyup, and retained-window timestamps share one browser timebase
if_missing: the report can only say the delay curve changes near 1000ms, not which ordering boundary it crosses

separates: V8/runtime-call, task-queue, microtask, input-priority, or protocol-checkpoint state
does_not_separate: CPU frequency, QoS, cache, product workload, or public API compatibility
acceptance_rule: sidecar-on/off rows preserve ordering; retained-key windows join to protocol commands, task categories, scheduler/input-priority fields, process/thread ids, and trace configuration
if_missing: runtime mechanism remains empirical and unnamed
collector: trace-off protocol sidecar, then scheduler/runtime trace

separates: whether browser, renderer, helper, and collector rows describe the same retained key window
acceptance_rule: driver/browser clocks are calibrated, renderer pid/thread/frame ids are stable, and every retained key joins to exactly one target window
if_missing: counter or trace rows are unjoinable even if they look correlated

separates: frequency, core residency, process QoS/tier, runnable latency, power, thermal, and scheduler/cache hypotheses
does_not_separate: Gutenberg source semantics, public subscriber compatibility, or product workload representativeness
acceptance_rule: accepted sidecar rows plus root counters separate slow no-CPU/background rows from fast ordinary/utility rows without changing ordering
if_missing: system mechanism remains empirical CPU-state sensitivity
collector: root powermetrics first, root trace fallback if needed
prerequisite: retained-key sidecar acceptance and root permission

separates: whether startup or pattern wait savings move setup/resource/actionability work into measurement
acceptance_rule: candidate wait arms retain failures, retries, resources, preview/canvas state, actionability waits, first-key tails, run order, and environment metadata
if_missing: a lower q50 can be mistaken for a safe CI wait reduction
collector: real Performance Tests artifact plus resource/actionability sidecar

separates: source-cost attribution versus behavior regression for selector guards
acceptance_rule: behavior fixtures pass before timing is interpreted; targeted owner spans collapse in count/time; aggregate p50 is secondary
if_missing: aggregate timing movement can be credited to the wrong source or a behavior change
collector: source-span microscope plus behavior fixture matrix

separates: whether fanout reduction preserves registry.subscribe, useSelect, withSelect, dynamic dependency, and persistence selector semantics
acceptance_rule: public/plugin subscriber fixtures pass while marker-only fanout collapses in the same prototype lane
if_missing: private or internal wins can be misreported as public-compatible data-layer changes
collector: compatibility matrix plus marker-only source spans

field_bundle: Workload stratum and semantic assertion fields
separates: whether fixed-x benchmark behavior transfers to real editing histories, plugin-heavy sessions, IME/composition, patterns, media, and idle return
acceptance_rule: each stratum has behavior assertions, event history, source spans, failures, retained rows, and environment metadata
if_missing: fixed-character evidence can be overgeneralized to product latency

separates: Chromium-internal screenshot/paint/drawframe versus semantic glyph, present timestamp, or camera-visible display timing
does_not_separate: source safety, CPU mechanism, or CI policy
acceptance_rule: external endpoint joins to retained keys, reports calibration error and dropped frames, and preserves observer-off ordering
if_missing: internal visual endpoint evidence can be overclaimed as physical display latency

separates: whether repository q50 movement maps to pass/fail, noisy-metric handling, or reviewer action
acceptance_rule: archived CI artifacts join raw rows, displayed q50, dashboard thresholds, review outcome, and noisy-metric policy
if_missing: local q50 can be misreported as CI pass/fail authority
collector: CI artifact archive plus dashboard/reviewer metadata
